source: USDA Economic Research Service (public domain). Primary: Food Availability (Per Capita) Data System (FADS), non-loss-adjusted 'Food Availability' tables (farm weight). Gaps filled from ERS Vegetables and Pulses Outlook VGS-375 and ERS Charts of Note; a few entries are secondary (The Packer quoting ERS/USDA) and flagged in their note and source.
notes: The basis is NOT loss-adjusted. The LAFA vegetables CSV (https://www.ers.usda.gov/media/5397/vegetables.csv, LAFA latest year 2022) has 16 attributes per commodity, and the fetch tool only returned the first ~2 commodities (artichokes, asparagus). The non-LAFA Food Availability tables were used instead. LAFA 'consumed' amounts are roughly 30-60% lower than these availability figures.
Farm-weight availability is close to garden harvest weight, which suits a harvest cap, but it is a supply-and-disappearance proxy, not measured intake.

dataYear 2022 is the FADS vegetable year. Each entry has an extra 'year' key, and some differ: fruit is 2021 (the FADS fruit update of 4/14/2023 ends at 2021); VGS-375 items are 2024; Packer-sourced items are 2023; processed snap beans, sweet corn, green peas and spinach are 2019, because ERS left 2020-2022 blank (NASS processing data suppressed or discontinued).
Each entry has an extra 'source' array naming the exact table(s) or document(s) its numbers came from.

Where the fresh and processed figures share a year and source, 'total' is our arithmetic sum of the ERS components. Otherwise 'total' is null rather than mixing years or bases. Where ERS publishes only a fresh series, total = fresh, and the note says so.

Numbers were read through a WebFetch text extractor from ERS CSVs, because direct download of ers.usda.gov was blocked by this session's egress proxy (403) and the .xlsx/.zip files came back as binary. Every FADS value used was confirmed by at least two independent extractions or cross-checked against another ERS table (e.g., canned and frozen potatoes match the potato table; the potato total of 110.62 matches VGS-370's 110.7). Values are rounded to 2 decimals from the full-precision ERS values.
Values that come from ERS outlook text (VGS-375: tomato, lettuce, onion, sweet potato, squash, pumpkin) are rounded by ERS to whole or one-decimal pounds.

Secondary-source values (The Packer) should be treated as provisional: spinach fresh, radish, snap bean fresh (2023, ERS Vegetables and Pulses Yearbook), and strawberry and raspberry (2021, 'USDA', basis unstated).
